source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Discard a partial controlled-substance dose without documentation whenever the remaining amount is too small to give.","B":"Assume federal law requires the same two-nurse witness process for every bedside waste event in every jurisdiction.","C":"Record only the administered portion and omit the remainder, because waste records do not affect controlled-substance records.","D":"Follow applicable law and facility policy for prompt waste, documentation, witnessing when required, and reconciliation."}}
source_row.rationale: Controlled-substance waste must be handled and documented under applicable federal, state/local and institutional requirements. A universal federal rule requiring the same second-nurse witness for every bedside partial dose should not be asserted without the governing policy.
source_row.source_detail: DEA disposal/destruction guidance explains practitioner responsibilities and controlled-substance disposal pathways; healthcare-facility procedures also operate under applicable state/local requirements and institutional controls. Current DEA Diversion Control drug-disposal Q&A rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A partial dose of a controlled substance must be discarded after administration. Which approach is most accurate?
